scope: M1 external watchdog ownership cleanup. Native macOS arm64 Node24 and emulated Linux x64 Node24; functional evidence only. The engine binary is unchanged from the storage checkpoint.

implementation.policy: Stop owned parent identities before descendants; allow orphan cleanup before promotion, including a zombie parent in the first snapshot. Escalate stuck owners individually, then the remaining whole tree.
implementation.limit: Process-query and scheduling overhead can extend nominal intervals. Descendants that cannot finish cleanup before forced escalation remain an explicitly reported failure; arbitrary guardian termination is not a promise of profile recovery.

additionalRegressions: SIGTERM-ignoring deep tree with bounded whole-tree escalation
CPU reset and PID reuse accounting

retainedFailures.assessment: The native full lifecycle batch exceeded its unchanged 240-second job budget after two existing recovery-case errors. Staged shutdown completed without an observed process/profile residue. This is not a suite pass.

The Linux full core batch exceeded its unchanged 240-second lifecycle budget after an existing context-close case failure. Its stopped-container audit found no owned profile. The full Linux matrix remains incomplete.
A deterministic regression reproduced immediate signalling of the guardian when the initial root snapshot was a zombie. The final policy grants the initial grace period to that state.

An initial synthetic stopped-parent test assumed SIGTERM could not terminate a stopped macOS process. The fixture now explicitly ignores SIGTERM to require escalation on both platforms. The initial run was not a pass.

failureRechecks.assessment: All three suspect existing renderer/keyboard/context-close cases passed separately on both platforms before the final zombie-only watchdog correction. Heavy shared-host activity was observed; it is a possible contributor, not a proven explanation of the full-batch failures. Their logs remain retained.

remaining: Complete full Linux verification and remaining lifecycle coverage under representative conditions; preserved timed-out batches are not passes.
